clue.text: Report from outlaw on edge of greenwood

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

indicators.note: the edge of the word greenwood is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Something is reported from an outlaw lurking at the edge of a forest, Robin Hood style.
explanation.definitionFit: A bang is a loud explosive noise, the sense in which a gunshot is a report.

clue.text: More dice being cast? It's no great shakes!

indicators.note: dice being cast are thrown and tumble at random, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone rolling extra dice declares the result unimpressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cast' rearranges MOREDICE; 'It's' is a link, leaving the idiom as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no great shakes is merely ordinary, of middling quality, which is this adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Poetry from Black Sea port lacking sex appeal

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letters for sex appeal are taken away from the port

parts.note: Odessa is a Ukrainian port on the Black Sea

explanation.surface: Verse comes from a Black Sea port that has no allure.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject are a classic form of poetry, collectively a body of verse.

clue.text: JFK formerly unemployed? Crazy!

parts.note: someone out of work is idle
crazy means wild

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the former JFK was out of work, then exclaims how mad that is.
explanation.walkthrough: JFK here is New York's airport, not the president: it was named Idlewild before 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: New York's John F Kennedy International Airport was called Idlewild until it was renamed after the assassination.

clue.text: Indian worker raising fruit, quite content

indicators.note: used as a noun, content means what is held inside, so the word for quite sits within
in a down clue raising lifts the word upwards, so the fruit is read bottom to top

parts.note: a haw is the fruit of the hawthorn
quite in the sense of entirely means all

explanation.surface: An Indian labourer, happy enough, is growing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as happy in the surface but is used as a noun, what something holds; 'raising' works upward because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In Indian English a wallah is a person employed in a particular job, as in tea-wallah.

clue.text: Mad Hatter's odd, having little time to run

indicators.note: mad suggests things thrown into disorder, so the letters of the following words are scrambled

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter from Alice is strange and always short of time, like the White Rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges HATTERSODD; the possessive's S is a letter of the fodder here. The surface borrows Alice in Wonderland's Mad Hatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-dated bond or product has only a brief period left before it matures or expires.

clue.text: The city of Orlando's a pleasant part in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back in time suggests reading the section backwards
part signals that a section of the following words is lifted out

explanation.surface: The setter Orlando calls part of his town pleasant, looking back on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' takes OSAPLE from 'Orlando's a pleasant' and 'in retrospect' reads it backwards; 'of' is a link. Orlando is the setter's own name, so the US city Orlando is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: El Paso is a city in Texas on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Win over, for example, taking wickets

indicators.note: taking means holding in, so the word for an example takes in the wicket letter

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example, so it means for example
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wickets

explanation.surface: A cricket side wins, for example, by taking wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway someone is to persuade them to your side, to win them over.

clue.text: Leading man in 13 across ignoring the odds

indicators.note: the pronoun for a man goes inside the remaining even letters
dropping the odd-numbered letters of the 13 across answer leaves only the even ones

parts.note: the cross-reference stands for the answer to that clue, the rum
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: It looks like it asks for the star of some play or film called 13 across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading man' looks like an actor in a show called 13 across, but splits into the definition and the pronoun. 'ignoring the odds' keeps the even letters of the rum's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ahead is to be in front, as a leading runner is.

clue.text: Who tabled amendment for coup de grâce?

indicators.note: an amendment changes a motion's wording, so here the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A committee asks who put forward the change that killed the motion off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amendment' rearranges WHOTABLED; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup de grâce is a final finishing strike, a killing blow.

clue.text: Female novelist has it in for Labour leader

indicators.note: has it in tells us the two letters are placed inside the novelist's name

parts.note: Elizabeth Gaskell was a Victorian novelist, author of Cranford

explanation.surface: A woman novelist has a grudge against a Labour Party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has it in for' looks like the idiom for bearing a grudge; 'in' is the container signal and 'has' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Gaitskell led the British Labour Party from 1955 to 1963.

clue.text: Set for scan and playback?

annotationWithheld.why: Set for scan and playback? (5): READ (scan) + Y, the back of 'play'; the single printed word 'playback' is both the fodder 'play' and the indicator 'back', one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Centre of attraction in pub: policeman providing rum

indicators.note: the middle letters are placed in the word for a pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: the centre of the word attraction is its two middle letters

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a police rank

explanation.surface: In a pub, a policeman is the centre of attention for supplying rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AC, the middle of 'attraction', into BAR as B-AC-AR; 'providing' is a link. 'Centre of attraction' looks like the idiom for the focus of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacardi is a well-known brand of rum, so it is an example of the spirit.

clue.text: Game birds brought to book

indicators.note: the birds are brought up to the book letter and attached after it

parts.note: owls are birds

explanation.surface: Game birds that have been shot are brought to account, as if before a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game birds' reads as one phrase but splits; 'brought to book' is an idiom for being punished.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowls is a game of rolling weighted balls towards a small target ball, the jack.

clue.text: Plant in Herts reorganised by director

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the pointer beside the jumbled county
reorganised means arranged differently, so the letters of the county are mixed up

parts.note: an arrow directs you the way to go, so it is a director

explanation.surface: A plant in Hertfordshire has been rearranged by the person running things.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is short for Hertfordshire, an English county. 'reorganised' turns HERTS into RESTH; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Restharrow is a European wild plant of the pea family with tough roots that once hindered harrows.

clue.text: Retreat from announcement of great uncertainty

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: great means high and uncertainty means doubt

explanation.surface: Someone backs away from a declaration full of doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding place where one can lie low is a retreat from the world.

clue.text: Timber frames with slight modification

indicators.note: to frame is to surround, so the timber goes round the letter for with

parts.note: teak is a hardwood timber

explanation.surface: Wood surrounds something that has been lightly altered, like a picture reframed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a small adjustment or fine-tuning change.

clue.text: Birds start to run in all directions

indicators.note: the opening of the run goes inside the compass letters

parts.note: W, E, N and S are the four compass points, taken here in that order

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A flock of birds starts to scatter everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrens are small brown songbirds with upturned tails.

clue.text: Dopey given short change in America

indicators.note: short tells us the coin's name is cut by its last letter

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin, small change

explanation.surface: A dozy person in the US has been given too little change.
explanation.walkthrough: Dopey sounds like the dwarf, but here it is just the definition: a dim person is slow-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim means slow-witted or dull, a near synonym of dopey.

clue.text: Yorkshire beauty queen, we hear, pulls the wool over one's eyes

definitions.text: pulls the wool over one's eyes

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is to be heard, not spelled

parts.note: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, so its beauty contest winner would be Miss Leeds

explanation.surface: A beauty queen from northern England is a deceiver.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull the wool over someone's eyes is to deceive them, which this verb means.

clue.text: 12 on time for food

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the cross-referenced word follows the time letter

parts.note: the answer to 12 across means fully prepared, which ripe also means

explanation.surface: A cross-reference sits on time for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 12 across answer READY gives RIPE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle, eaten as food.

clue.text: Up in arms about leaders of Nicaraguan group aided in scandal

indicators.note: about means around, so the angry word is placed round the leading letters

parts.note: someone up in arms is irate, angry

indicators.note: the leaders of the three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Anger about a Nicaraguan rebel group that was helped in a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts NGA into IRATE as IRA-NGA-TE; 'in' is a link. The 1980s Iran-Contra affair involved US arms for Iran funding Nicaraguan rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: Irangate was the media name for the Iran-Contra political scandal under Reagan.

clue.text: Topper recollected his talk

indicators.note: read as re-collected, gathered up again in another order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A person in a top hat remembers what he said.
explanation.definitionFit: A topper is a tall formal top hat made of silk plush.

clue.text: Nothing to support listed building extension

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes below, so the zero is placed under

parts.note: a ship that listed leaned over, so it leant
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is there to prop up an extension on a protected listed building.
explanation.walkthrough: A listed building in Britain is one protected for historic interest; here 'listed' means leant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed or extension built against a wall with a sloping roof.

clue.text: Tasteless articles about one computer game

indicators.note: about means round, placing the cheap goods round the letters

parts.note: tat is cheap tasteless goods
I is the Roman numeral one
PC is a personal computer

explanation.surface: Cheap articles about a single computer game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'computer game' reads as one phrase, but 'game' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipcat is an old children's game in which a tapered stick is struck and hit away.

clue.text: Regrettable dismissal of American loser

parts.note: a regrettable event is sad
getting the sack is dismissal from a job

explanation.surface: A sorry firing of an American failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sad sack is US slang for an inept, hapless person who always fails.

clue.text: Naturally a gift is left for blonde to accept

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the fair word takes in the letter for left

parts.note: fair hair is blonde

explanation.surface: A gift that comes naturally is abandoned for a blonde to receive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'for' are links; 'left' is not the verb but L.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural talent or aptitude, an inborn gift.

clue.text: Get hot under the collar following Australian runner — not down under!

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: not down means up, so in this down clue the bird is read upwards; down under also hints at Australia

parts.note: the emu is a flightless Australian bird that runs

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry chasing an Australian runner who is not in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not down under' turns EMU into UME, under F.
explanation.definitionFit: To fume is to seethe with anger, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Film director first to include song? Not so!

indicators.note: to include is to hold within, so the first word holds the remainder

parts.note: premier means first

indicators.note: not so says the two letters are taken out of the word before

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A director is the first to put a song in a film, or so he insists not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' reads as a denial but takes two letters out of the song. Otto Preminger directed Laura and Anatomy of a Murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto Preminger was an Austrian-American film director.

clue.text: Russian leader in bed, topless

indicators.note: topless in a down clue removes the top letter

parts.note: a divan is a kind of bed

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler lying in bed without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan the Terrible was the first tsar of Russia, a famous Russian ruler.

clue.text: Red inside like gold dust

definitions.meaning: meat cooked so it is still red in the middle
very scarce and hard to come by

explanation.definitionFit: Rare meat is barely cooked and red within, and rare also means scarce, as gold dust is.

clue.text: Chap bumped into at first in London suburbs

indicators.note: the encounter word comes first, ahead of the man's name

parts.note: if you met someone you bumped into them
Roland is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man was encountered first in the London suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. Metroland was the name for the suburbs northwest of London built along the Metropolitan Railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Metro-land is the name for the commuter suburbs served by London's Metropolitan line.

clue.text: Flower expert needing no introduction

indicators.note: needing no introduction drops the first letter, the opening of the word

parts.note: a master is an expert

explanation.surface: A flower expert so famous they need no introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Asters are daisy-like flowering plants such as Michaelmas daisies.
